B: Optimal replacement algorithm (Belady) minimizes misses for given cache size, but cannot guarantee 100% hit rate generally because working set larger than cache or compulsory misses? Also first reference compulsory miss. So false.
C: Cache itself speed faster -> equivalent access speed faster? Equivalent access time depends on hit rate, cache access time, main memory access time, miss penalty. If cache speed increases (cache access time lower), equivalent speed faster, assuming hit rate not degraded? In general, cache speed faster improves performance; "本身的速度越快，则Cache存储器的等效访问速度就越快" likely true? Need verify: Equivalent access speed = 1/(hit rate * cache access time + miss rate * memory access time?) If cache speed faster, cache access time decreases, average access time decreases. So true.
D: Larger difference between cache and main memory capacity? The capacity ratio? Cache smaller than memory; difference? "差别越大越好" not necessarily; cache should be sufficiently large to improve hit rate but constrained by cost/speed. Too large cache may be slower/more expensive, and not necessarily better. False.
